description:
Basic RIP (Routing Information Protocol) configuration across 4 routers in a small enterprise network. Configure RIPv2 with network statements, enable authentication, and verify full routing table convergence. RIP is a distance-vector protocol covered in CCNA curriculum as a foundational routing protocol concept.

IP Addressing Plan (configure these IPs on the routers):
- R1: eth1=10.1.1.1/30, eth2=10.1.2.1/30, lo=10.0.0.1/32
- R2: eth1=10.1.1.2/30, eth2=10.2.1.1/30, lo=10.0.0.2/32
- R3: eth1=10.1.2.2/30, eth2=10.3.1.1/30, lo=10.0.0.3/32
- R4: eth1=10.2.1.2/30, eth2=10.3.1.2/30, lo=10.0.0.4/32

properties.description: RIP process is running on R1
R1 has learned RIP routes from neighbors
End-to-end reachability: R1 can reach R4 via learned RIP routes

optimal_solution.description: Configure IP addresses on all interfaces, enter RIP configuration mode, specify version 2, add network statements for directly connected networks, verify routing table convergence

research_context.citation: CCNA 200-301 curriculum covers RIP as foundational distance-vector protocol. RIP configuration is simpler than OSPF (single-area OSPF: 20-40min, RIP typically 15-25min for basic configs). CCNA exam sims target 5-10 minutes per task for proficient candidates. RIP is covered in Cisco CCNA official cert guide chapter on distance-vector routing.
research_context.literature_basis: RIP is a standard CCNA topic covered in Cisco CCNA 200-301 official certification guide. While RIP is considered legacy, it's still taught as the simplest distance-vector protocol for understanding routing fundamentals. FRR fully supports RIPv1/v2 (RFC 2453). Common CCNA lab exercises include basic RIP configuration with network statements and RIPv2 authentication.
research_context.time_justification: 20 minutes is reasonable for basic RIP configuration. RIP is simpler than OSPF (no areas, no adjacency states beyond basic neighbor discovery). CCNA practice: basic RIP configs 15-25min for novices. Aligns with CCNA exam sim format (5-10min target for proficient users). FRR RIP configuration uses similar commands to Cisco IOS.
research_context.platform_notes: FRR fully supports RIP and RIPv2. Commands are similar to Cisco IOS: 'router rip', 'version 2', 'network X.X.X.X/X'. FRR RIP implementation is RFC 2453 compliant.
